findings.body:
The new field `reasoning_effort` is cloned from `models.reasoning_effort` on line 75, but I was unable to confirm that `Models` (the config type that `models()` constructs in the test) actually has a `reasoning_effort` field.  If the config struct does not contain this field, the line compiles into a dead-code path and the setting is silently ignored – the exact failure mode described in the removed comment for `max_tokens`.

When the repository’s `Models` struct is defined reliably as carrying `reasoning_effort: String`, this finding should be closed.  If it does not, the change introduces a configuration parameter that is discarded before use.

Fix: add the field to `Models`, or remove the clone and the field from `GatewayModel` and keep reasoning hard-disabled.
findings.title: Verify that `Models.reasoning_effort` exists outside the diff

lookups.why: The diff reads `models.reasoning_effort.clone()` on line 75 and constructs `Models { reasoning_effort: "high".into(), … }` in the test.  This lookup confirms whether the config struct actually carries that field.

value.summary: The change re-enables OpenRouter reasoning at a configurable effort level, with well-separated concerns and unit tests.  I could not verify that `Models.reasoning_effort` exists in the repository’s config types, which is the critical glue between the new field and its use – if that field does not exist, the addition is dead code and the map match never reaches the new `reasoning_effort` line.  No other bugs were found in the visible logic.
